title: Schema Drift: Silent Field Loss on Read-Modify-Write (SILENT_FIELD_LOSS)
pattern: An application decodes an incoming object using a local structural type that only represents a subset of the fields in the datastore, modifies a field, and writes the object back to the datastore by complete clobbering/overwrite.
why_bad: It breaks forward-compatibility during rolling deployments. When newer instances write records containing newer schema extensions, any interleaved write by an older-version instance will silently purge the unrecognized fields, causing severe data loss.
detection: Observe cases where a deserialized DTO is serialized back into the exact same database record by an complete overwrite statement, without preserving or mapping unknown fields into an internal buffer.
fix: Flatten unknown elements into an intermediate map buffer during deserialization and merge them back when writing, or run targeted delta/field-level updates (e.g., `UPDATE ... SET`) instead of full document clobbering.
source: *Martin Kleppmann - Designing Data-Intensive Applications (2017)*, Chapter 4 (Figure 4-7); *Vaughn Vernon - Implementing Domain-Driven Design (2013)*, Chapter 14.
